messages.subject: c to R interface bug?
parts:
Hey,
I am fitting another event time model with a large dataset (99184 rows) that has routinely crashed R with no error messages. I truncated the data (70 rows) to fewer years to exactly match an analysis done years ago and finally received some error messages. I am recreating this analysis, eventually with a decade of new data.  Consequently, I know this model works and that it can be run with 2009 computers using winbugs.

The model is structured to be expanded into a spatial model, so looks a bit weird, but is ultimately an intercept model with a single parameter beta0.

modelcode = nimbleCode({
  beta0 ~ dflat()
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in (runsum[i]+1):runsum[i+1]) { 
      for (k in 1:agem[j]) {
        gamma[j,k]<-(beta0)
        dayhaz[j,k] <- exp(gamma[j,k])
      } #k
      icumhaz[j]<-sum(dayhaz[j,1:agem[j]])
      p[j] <-1-exp(-icumhaz[j])
      pos[j] ~ dbern(p[j])
    } #j
  } #i
})#end model

The model compiles, mcmc runs, then poof error message appears or else R just crashes.

The error messages I've received have been on both the nimble/R side and with a C++ namespace error.

(1) When the model was run using the large dataset using nimbleMCMC with 200000 iterations, I received a nimble/R error:

Error in eval(call(".Call", nimbleUserNamespace$sessionSpecificDll$matrix2VecNim
Arr,  :
  long vectors not supported yet: memory.c:3451


(2) When this same model was run using subsetted data with nimbleMCMC with 100000 iterations, I received a c++ error that then crashed R:

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_array_new_length'
  what():  std::bad_array_new_length
Aborted (core dumped)


Not sure what to do these errors, or what they mean exactly. Googling suggests that given the large data, perhaps I'm exceeding R limits with respect to matrix size. But the namespace error is perhaps the actual bug? Since this is the least complex model we are planning to use, it's a bit troublesome to have a possible size limit problem.


Thanks for any help you could provide!

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: c to R interface bug?
parts:
Dear nimble-users,

Thanks for Alison for following up with me off-list with her example.  Here is a summary for interested readers of the situation:

The requested samples were > 75Gb.  Although it was being run on a machine with more memory than that, still it seems to be above R's memory limitations.  There is material online about changing R's memory limits.

We were able to make the model faster to build and probably to run by removing dayhaz and replacing icumhaz with icumhaz[j] <- sum(exp(gamma[j, 1:agem[j]])).  We left gamma there as a placeholder for a more complicated model component.  It would also be possible to remove icumhaz[j] and caculate p[j] in a single expression.  In other situations, one can remove large intermediate variables from model code by writing user-defined functions as nimbleFunctions.

We discourage an unnecessary for loop like the loop for i in this case.  Other software does not generate an error in such cases.

The error reported involving matrix2VecNim can only occur when using WAIC=TRUE with multiple chains.  If that were the only issue, it could be avoided by WAIC = FALSE or using only one chain.  However, it seems to go hand-in-hand with requesting huge MCMC samples.  We don't have a case where this error is triggered except in this context of overall too much memory use, although in theory it could be possible.

-Perry
